subject: Cerulean Health — prioritization ask and decision framework
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cerulean prioritization — can we scope a lean path?

Team —

Cerulean Health (large prospect; enterprise security + regional residency requirements) is asking us to commit to two deliverables as part of a Q4 commitment if we want to close:

1) Tenant-level routing: ensure traffic from specific Cerulean tenant is pinned to a US-only residency pool (customer-managed residency preference).
2) Audit export window extension: nightly export of full request/response traces + redaction metadata (current system exports only 30 days; they want 365).

Ben and I need to assemble an internal ask for Product/Eng — they expect a firm timeline in the SOW they just shared (attached). They will consider a multi-year committed contract but want these features in the first 90 days post-signing.

Asks:
- Dev: quick feasibility + blockers and an honest estimate for an MVP (what minimal work gets us to a safe SOW-level promise?).
- Michael: where can this sit in roadmap? any existing work we can re-use?
- Priyom/Ben: any willingness from Cerulean to fund a dedicated engineering track or acceptance of a phased delivery?

I expect a short internal decision today so I can push back to Sarah with a pragmatic offer.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Global Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean prioritization — can we scope a lean path?

Marissa —

High level: both requests are doable but with different risk and infra surface area. Quick notes:

1) Tenant-level routing (US-only residency pool)
- Work: routing policy + tenancy tag + control-plane flag + capacity reservations on US hosts. We already have per-tenant affinity code, but not a customer-facing residency toggle.
- Estimated MVP effort: ~3-4 full-time engineer-weeks + infra work for capacity reservations and config UI gating.
- Risk: medium — requires changes to scheduling and fallback so we don't break scaling guarantees.

2) Audit export window extension (30 -> 365 days)
- Work: storage policy + cost/retention UI + compliance filter + audit redaction pipeline. We already export traces to a cold bucket; the change is mostly retention and redaction policy plus adding a per-customer retention config.
- Estimated MVP effort: ~2 engineer-weeks + SRE coordination and cost projection.
- Risk: low-medium (cost is the biggest concern).

If they need both in 90 days, we can do a phased approach: retention change first (lower effort) and residency toggle as a paid priority.

I can draft a concise tech note for the SOW that states: phased delivery with retention in 30 days after sign, residency toggle in 90 days contingent on capacity reservation and optional paid engineering track.

- Dev

On Thu, Oct 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> (see above)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean prioritization — can we scope a lean path?

Short context: Cerulean is at POC completion and legal/finance are engaged. Their exec sponsor (CTO) has committed to a purchase if we can guarantee the two items in the SOW. They have a strong preference for US residency due to a pending audit from a payer partner.

They have signaled willingness to:
- Pay a one-time engineering escrow (they called it a "delivery fee") if we need a dedicated sprint.
- Accept a phased rollout if we put a binding commitment in the SOW for the first deliverable (retention) and a second-binding timeline (residency) tied to a paid capacity reservation.

My ask: can we get a crisp two-option proposal to present to Sarah today:
A) Standard SOW: retention -> 30d to 365d in 30 days; residency in 90 days on paid path.
B) Accelerated (paid): residency delivered in 45 days for a delivery fee + committed capacity purchase.

I can push the procurement conversation if we have these timelines.

- Ben

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean prioritization — can we scope a lean path?

Thanks for the context. A few product roadmap notes and a proposed decision framework: 

- Roadmap capacity: Q4 sprint allocations are partially filled; we have a small slot for security/compliance features and a separate infra reliability sprint. I can defer a low-risk item into that slot but high-risk scheduler changes will need a paid priority or a trade for an existing infra ticket.

- Decision framework (what I need to sign off):
  * Impact: ARR and strategic value (Cerulean is strategic for our payer vertical).
  * Cost & runway: engineering effort + ongoing cost delta (365-day retention increases storage bill).
  * Risk: rollout complexity and ability to gracefully degrade.

Give me the following by EOD and I can commit to a route:
1) Concrete list of what goes into the MVP for each ask (Dev, please bullet).
2) A proposed commercial structure (Ben) — which option we recommend and what Cerulean would pay.
3) Legal/Procurement constraints from Cerulean (Marissa) — anything non-standard in the SOW.

If we align quickly, I can slot the retention work into the Q4 compliance patch; residency toggle will need a priority lane unless we accept a 90+ day timeline.

- Michael
Product Manager, Core Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@ceruleanhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ceruleanhealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW v2 and timeline questions

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick call last week. Attaching SOW_v2 (Cerulean_SOW_v2.pdf) — section 3 lists the two deliverables we need in our kickoff window. We are open to a phased acceptance but the payer audit is scheduled for mid-December so retention must be completed early.

Two clarifications for your internal team: 
- Retention must include redaction metadata exports (PII redaction markers) so our audit team can validate compliance.
- Residency toggle must prevent any routing fallback to non-US pools for the tenant during normal operation; fallbacks are acceptable during DR events only if documented.

We can commit to a three-year contract and are prepared to include a one-time delivery fee if that reduces timeline risk. Please send a proposed SOW timeline by EOD Oct 22.

Best,
Sarah Liu
VP of IT & Security
Cerulean Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cerulean prioritization — proposed reply to Cerulean

Team —

Thanks for the rapid turn. Based on inputs, draft proposal we should send to Sarah (short & binding):

Option A (standard):
- Retention & redaction metadata export delivered within 30 days of signature.
- Residency toggle: delivery commitment within 90 days; activation requires customer purchase of a US capacity reservation (we'll include the price in the SOW).
- No delivery fee; standard support SLA.

Option B (accelerated / paid):
- Retention & redaction metadata export within 14 days of signature.
- Residency toggle delivered within 45 days with a delivery fee of $125k and a committed 12-month reserved capacity (terms in proposal).

We will attach a short tech appendix (Dev) that describes the MVP scope and rollback semantics. Michael — please approve the routing of the residency toggle into a paid priority lane (I can commit to the commercial terms if you approve technical feas.).

Ben — can you draft the SOW note and update the HubSpot deal with Option B as a close plan? I will send the two-option email to Sarah after we align.

Marissa
Senior Director, Global Sales
Redwood Inference
